policy_change_risk_reason: No negative change since 2022 was identified in reviewed official sources. Current MIT pages still state need-blind admissions for all students and 100% demonstrated-need treatment for international students. Endowed funds remain very large, though external macro pressures remain a general watch item.

computed.implied_gap: ESTIMATE: USD 15,494 using current 2026-2027 COA of USD 92,760; comparable-year proxy gap is USD 12,074 using official USD 89,340 cost figure
computed.pct_coa_covered_by_avg: ESTIMATE: 83.3% using current 2026-2027 COA; comparable-year proxy is 86.5% using USD 89,340

cds.avg_loan_component: USD 0 on required-package basis according to MIT's no-required-loan packaging statement; actual voluntary international borrowing average is DATA NOT PUBLICLY AVAILABLE
cds.work_study_in_package: Student employment exists, but Federal Work-Study does not generally apply to international students; most MIT students make about USD 1,700 per term from campus work

bangladesh_specific.estimated_annual_admits: ESTIMATE: roughly 1-2 Bangladeshi undergraduates per entering class, inferred from 6-8 Bangladeshi undergraduates enrolled in 2024-2026 official ISO country counts
bangladesh_specific.documentation_notes: MIT has an international-specific aid page, accepts local-country tax documents with non-professional English translation, uses CSS Profile plus IDOC, may request CSS Business/Farm Supplement, and assigns financial aid counselors. No Bangladesh-specific documentation page was found.

clutch_programs.name: MIT Scholarship
clutch_programs.deadline: Follows MIT financial aid application deadlines: November 30 for Early Action and February 15 for Regular Action
clutch_programs.notes: Automatic consideration through CSS Profile plus IDOC; median MIT Scholarship was USD 69,777 in 2024-2025; awarded solely on financial need.

clutch_programs.name: First Year Grant
clutch_programs.notes: For highest-need first-year students; intended for transition costs.

clutch_programs.name: QuestBridge National College Match
clutch_programs.deadline: QuestBridge calendar; MIT supplement and aid materials by November 1 for ranked finalists
clutch_programs.notes: Important limitation: QuestBridge says international students living outside the U.S. are not eligible. So this is not usable for a Bangladesh-based applicant.

reachability.notes: These are ESTIMATES, not MIT published probabilities. They are anchored to MIT's 1.96% international admit rate for the Class of 2029, MIT's admitted-score ranges, and MIT's very high likelihood of substantial need-based funding once a high-need student is admitted. Methodology schema bins are sat_1300 and sat_1400; in the report these correspond to the requested 1350 and 1430 bands.

endowment_stability.endowment_per_student: ESTIMATE: about USD 2.316 million per student using USD 27.3662 billion endowed funds and 11,816 students
endowment_stability.policy_change_last_5yr: No negative international-aid policy change was identified in reviewed official sources. Current 2026 pages continue to state need-blind admissions for all students and 100% demonstrated-need treatment for international students.

admissions.early_decision_reason: MIT does not offer Early Decision. It offers non-binding Early Action and Regular Action, and MIT explicitly says there is no strategic benefit to one cycle over the other.
admissions_values: Academic readiness for MIT's General Institute Requirements
Strong preparation in calculus and quantitative science
Holistic admissions and match with MIT
Challenging humanities, arts, and social science coursework also matters

red_flags_for_bd_applicants: MIT does not explicitly name Bangladesh SSC/HSC on the reviewed admissions pages
No official WES/ECE requirement was found, but applicants must still provide formal school transcripts
Aid is re-evaluated annually rather than guaranteed as a fixed four-year package in the reviewed sources
Bangladesh-specific aid rate and package size are not publicly disclosed
QuestBridge is not available to students living in Bangladesh

verdicts.honest_summary: MIT is financially real for a high-need Bangladeshi student, but admission is the real bottleneck. If admitted and if the family's need is documented in a way MIT accepts, MIT is one of the strongest full-funding outcomes in the U.S.; if not admitted, the generosity is irrelevant.
verdicts.recommended_for_bd_student_profile: Recommended only as an ultra-reach for a very strong Bangladesh-based applicant, ideally with exceptional quantitative distinction, excellent testing, and a meticulously documented aid file.
clutch_factors_applicable: Clear contextualisation of rigorous SSC/HSC or A-Level coursework
Strong SAT or ACT plus English proof if relevant
Well-prepared CSS Profile and IDOC documentation with translations
Willingness to request aid review if MIT misreads family finances
key_risks: Annual aid reassessment rather than a fixed package guarantee
Bangladesh-specific aid outcomes are not publicly visible

data_gaps: Bangladesh-specific aid rate is not public
Bangladesh-specific average package amount is not public
Actual average loan take-up among aided international undergraduates is not published separately
No reviewed official source confirmed a Bangladeshi student association at MIT
No robust verified Bangladesh feeder-school pattern was found
contradictions: No material contradiction between MIT's published aid claims and the CDS was found. The main source split is that need-blind wording is explicit on the admissions FAQ, while the international-specific aid page states same-process and full-need treatment without repeating the term need-blind.
stale_data_flags: CDS H6 data are 2024-2025 estimated, not final
Current COA is 2026-2027, so comparisons against H6 require a year-mismatch caveat
Bangladesh enrollment counts are current for 2025-2026, but aid-by-country data are unavailable
data_quality.integrity_note: This profile is strongest on official policy, CDS, admissions, cost, and MIT ISO country counts. It is weaker on Bangladesh-specific anecdotal profiles, feeder-school patterns, and any granular country-by-country aid breakdown because MIT does not publish those details.
